questions.q: What does it mean that Purview glossary terms are "active" rather than static, per the lesson?
options: A policy attached to a term applies automatically to any data product the term is linked to
Terms automatically delete themselves after 90 days
Terms can only be edited by the tenant administrator
Active terms cannot be grouped under a governance domain
questions.explain: In Unified Catalog, terms carry policies — governance requirements and terms-of-use — that apply automatically wherever the term is attached, not just a static definition.

questions.q: What is the first step in creating a new glossary term?
options: Picking a term template, such as System default or a custom organization template
Publishing it directly to the Enterprise Glossary
Deleting the governance domain it will belong to
Assigning it a data quality score
questions.explain: New terms start by selecting a term template, which determines which fields the term will have — System default's basic fields, or a richer custom template.

questions.q: Put the term lifecycle stages in the correct order.
options: Draft, submitted for approval, published
Published, draft, submitted for approval
Submitted for approval, published, draft
Draft, published, submitted for approval
questions.explain: A term starts as Draft, is submitted for approval for a steward to review, and once approved becomes Published.

questions.q: For a term to actually appear in the Enterprise Glossary, what must be true?
options: Both the term itself and the governance domain it belongs to must be published
Only the term needs to be in Draft status
It only needs an Acronym field filled in
Nothing — all terms appear automatically regardless of status
questions.explain: If either the term or its parent governance domain is still in draft, the term stays hidden from the Enterprise Glossary — both must be published.

questions.q: Which field lets multiple shorthand versions of a term (like "CLV" and "Customer Lifetime Value") resolve to the same glossary entry?
options: Acronym
Data Privacy
Resources
Status
questions.explain: The Acronym field accepts comma-separated values, so shorthand forms of a term's name all map back to the same glossary entry.
